statement: For any canonical ordinary CNF with m clauses, if the selected minimum-incidence pivot has d=m-1, then every live variable is omitted from at most one clause. Let p,q be pivot polarity bucket sizes and a=min(p,q). There is exactly one retained clause. The number of distinct non-tautological resolvents is at most max(1,p*q-a+1), hence m'<=1+max(1,p*q-a+1).
proof: Minimum incidence d_min=m-1 implies every live variable has incidence at least m-1 and at most m, hence every live variable is omitted from at most one of the m clauses.
The selected pivot occurs in exactly m-1 clauses, so exactly one clause is retained.

Any positive-negative pivot-parent pair jointly covers every nonpivot live variable: no variable can be omitted from both parents because it is omitted from at most one clause total. Therefore every non-tautological resolvent is a full-width signed tail over all remaining live variables.

Let a=min(p,q), and assume without loss p=a<=q. If every nonpivot variable has a uniform sign across all pivot parents in which it appears, then every non-tautological cross-pair produces the same full-width signed tail, so there is at most one distinct resolvent.

Otherwise choose a nonpivot variable whose signs are nonuniform among pivot parents. If the p-side contains both signs, each present q-side parent conflicts with at least one p-side sign; since at most one parent omits the variable, there are at least q-1>=p-1=a-1 tautological cross-pairs. If the p-side is sign-uniform, nonuniformity forces at least one opposite-sign q-side parent, which conflicts with every present p-side parent; again at least p-1=a-1 pairs are tautological.
Hence in the nonuniform case at most p*q-(a-1)=p*q-a+1 cross-pairs are non-tautological, and distinct resolvents are no more numerous than those pairs.

Combining the uniform and nonuniform cases yields at most max(1,p*q-a+1) distinct resolvents. Adding the one retained clause proves m'<=1+max(1,p*q-a+1). Canonicalization can only reduce the count further.

useful_instance.note: The 5+5 split also gives 22; all other splits are smaller.
